commit_subject: (screen-flagged) Clarify boundary: NC charitable deduction now excludes the section 170 deduction attributable to a credit-backed donation rather than the donation value (scope of excluded amount).
other_kind: wrong_quantity_basis (excluded amount measured as the donation's value instead of the section 170 deduction attributable to it)
description: The independent cycle found and fixed signed-income flooring, MFS cap handling, the current charitable-deduction exclusion, incomplete boundary/status coverage, deduction-attribution semantics for credit-backed property, and an untested MFS under-cap branch.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: N.C. Gen. Stat. 105-153.5(a)(2)a bases the NC charitable deduction on "The amount allowed as a deduction for charitable contributions under section 170 of the Code for that taxable year" and sub-sub-subdivision 3 makes a credit-backed qualified donation ineligible for that deduction, so the amount to remove is the section 170 deduction attributable to the donation, whereas the pre-fix formula subtracted the donation's own value and therefore over-excluded whenever that donation's section 170 deduction is smaller than the donation amount (percentage limits, carryforwards, property valuation rules).
triage.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus release (us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix, corpus commit 01e00777cb, provision us-nc/statute/105/105-153.5); the operative text is quoted in pre_fix_wrong_because. The diff is a three-part semantic change to one rule: source string, formula subtrahend, and the renamed input nc_pit_2026_credit_backed_qualified_real_property_donation -> nc_pit_2026_section_170_deduction_attributable_to_credit_backed_donation, whose new description reads "Current-year federal section 170 deduction amount attributable to a qualified real-property donation that is the basis for an allocated section 105-153.11 credit; this deduction amount, rather than the donation's value, is excluded from the North Carolina charitable deduction." (usable as a module_comment quote if a reviewer prefers it). Proof-atom excerpt, effective dates, entity, period and outputs are unchanged, so this is not excerpt-only provenance. The subtrahend is a module input, so the fix changes the module's input contract rather than an internal derivation, but it is a genuine meaning change: the new fixture "limited credit-backed section 170 deduction preserves unrelated charitable deduction" (contributions 7000, attributable section 170 deduction 2000 -> eligible 5000) exercises exactly that distinction. Kind bucketing is the uncertain part: untraceable_branch is a near miss under its "value with no basis in the cited source ... re-grounds it" clause, but the pre-fix subtrahend did trace to carve-out 3 and was merely quantified on the wrong basis; wrong_entity_or_scope's listed senses (entity, population, filing status, geography, program scope, output surface) do not cover a mis-measured amount; so I used other. The commit subject also says "MFS deductions", but the MFS cap rule in the YAML is untouched - the MFS part of this commit is a new test fixture only. This is an in-branch fix inside merged PR #1023 (no reviews or review comments recorded). Two later commits touch the file (450ca0144 "Use canonical NC module source locator", d1ed1b594 "Repair NC TY2026 statute source backing"); both look like source/provenance repairs, not reversals.
triage.verifier_justification: The pinned corpus text of N.C. Gen. Stat. 105-153.5(a)(2)a sets the NC charitable base as "The amount allowed as a deduction for charitable contributions under section 170 of the Code for that taxable year," and sub-sub-subdivision 3 says only that "A qualified donation that is the basis for an allocated credit under G.S. 105-153.11 is not eligible for a deduction under this subdivision" — so the quantity to remove from that base is the section 170 deduction attributable to the donation, not the donation's own value. Pre-fix, the subtrahend input was documented as "Qualified real-property donation that is the basis for an allocated section 105-153.11 credit," i.e. the donation amount, so whenever the section 170 percentage-of-AGI limits or 170(e) basis reduction made the current-year deduction smaller than the donation, the module over-excluded and (through the max(0, ...) floor) could wipe out unrelated charitable deductions; the new fixture "limited credit-backed section 170 deduction preserves unrelated charitable deduction" (7000 contributions, 2000 attributable deduction, 5000 preserved) is exactly that case. No listed kind fits: no numeric literal, boundary strictness, clause, period, entity/population, or boolean operator changed, and the removed quantity was not untraceable (the statute does name the qualified donation) — it was the wrong measurement basis for the excluded amount, so "other: wrong_quantity_basis" is the honest kind. I could not refute the fidelity call: the pre-fix input semantics genuinely disagree with the cited text, and the fix re-states the excluded amount on the statute's own basis.
triage.verifier_notes: Strongest surviving counterargument, which a reviewer should weigh: the change is carried entirely by an input rename plus its `description` and the rule's `source:` string. The arithmetic shape is byte-identical (max(0, contributions - X)), no parameter, version window, effective date, entity, or boolean changed, and the test edits are a pure alpha-rename except the one added fixture, whose expected values would come out the same under the old semantics too (supplying 2000 as a donation value yields 5000 as well). So a strict "formula/parameter must change" reading could call this a contract/documentation clarification (mechanical-adjacent) rather than a computed-meaning change. I still land on confirmed because the input's documented quantity is part of the encoded meaning — a binder populating this module from federal data supplies a materially different number after the fix — and both the pre-fix description ("Qualified real-property donation ... and is therefore excluded from the deduction") and the post-fix one ("this deduction amount, rather than the donation's value, is excluded") state the two incompatible bases explicitly. Secondary notes: the proof atom's excerpt and citation path are unchanged, so this is not an excerpt-only/provenance edit; the commit's parenthetical "(scope of excluded amount)" tempts a wrong_entity_or_scope reading, but that kind covers entity/population/program/output scope, not the measurement basis of a money amount. The PR-body quote the first reader used ("deduction-attribution semantics for credit-backed property" inside the cycle sentence) is real but generic; the diff and the statute, not that sentence, are what settle the call. Commit also bundles an unrelated MFS-cap fixture addition, which is not part of this rule's defect.
